issues.title: shutil.which() called with string as mode argument in _sign_elf()
issues.description: In _sign_elf(), the fallback lookup `shutil.which("binary-sign-tool", f"{hnp_bin}/binary-sign-tool")` passes a string as the second positional argument, which is `mode` (expected int, default os.F_OK | os.X_OK), not `path`. If this code path is reached (i.e., binary-sign-tool is not at the default /data/service/hnp/bin/ location), os.access() will raise TypeError: an integer is required. This would crash the build. The correct form should be `shutil.which("binary-sign-tool") or f"{hnp_bin}/binary-sign-tool"` (matching the pattern already used for llvm-objcopy on the preceding line). Note: this bug is latent — it only triggers when the sign tool is absent from the default location, which did not occur during the reported build.
issues.recommendation: Change to: sign_tool = shutil.which("binary-sign-tool") or f"{hnp_bin}/binary-sign-tool"

issues.title: test_package only performs smoke test (duf --version); no platform-specific functionality verified
issues.description: R40 states that for system-level utilities (procfs/sysfs/netlink), test_package should cover platform-related functionality beyond a version() call. duf reads mount information from /proc/mounts or equivalent procfs/sysfs interfaces. The current test only runs `duf --version` and asserts the output contains 'duf'. While this satisfies R34 (genuine binary dependency), it does not verify that duf can actually enumerate disks on HarmonyOS. The upstream `go test ./...` is run in the CI build phase (documented in MANIFEST.yml), which partially mitigates this. For a pure Go application with CGO_ENABLED=0, the Go standard library handles procfs access, so no platform-specific patches are needed. This is a warning, not a blocker.
issues.recommendation: Consider adding a test that runs `duf` without arguments (or `duf --help`) and checks for non-empty output containing mount/disk information, to verify the binary can actually access HarmonyOS procfs/sysfs.

issues.title: manifest.yaml uses 'software:' instead of 'name:' as shown in code style rule
issues.description: Code style rule #14 shows the manifest.yaml format with `name: zlib`, but the actual file uses `software: duf`. This may be an intentional schema evolution, but it deviates from the documented example.
issues.recommendation: Verify whether the manifest schema has been updated to use 'software' instead of 'name'. If so, update the code style rule. If not, change to 'name: duf'.

issues.title: Inline imports inside methods instead of at module top level
issues.description: Several methods contain inline import statements: `import subprocess` (_find_go), `import io` (build), `import shutil`/`import subprocess`/`from pathlib import Path` (_sign_elf), `import time` (_sign_elf). Code style rule #16 specifies imports should follow stdlib → third-party → project order at the top of the file. The `import shutil` in _sign_elf is also redundant (already imported at top).
issues.recommendation: Move all imports to the top of the file following the standard ordering convention.

issues.title: url attribute points to upstream project rather than recipe repository
issues.description: In Conan convention, the `url` attribute typically points to the recipe's repository (where the conanfile.py is hosted), while `homepage` points to the upstream project. Here both are set to https://github.com/muesli/duf. This is common practice but technically the url should point to the recipe repo.
issues.recommendation: Consider setting url to the recipe repository URL if applicable, or document that the convention is to point url to upstream for single-package recipes.

issues.title: test.sh uses [test] marker instead of [step]
issues.description: Code style rule #9 specifies step markers should use `[step]`, success `[ok]`, failure `[fail]`. The script uses `[test]` as the marker instead of `[step]`. The `[ok]` and `[fail]` markers with 8-space indent are correct.
issues.recommendation: Change `[test]` to `[step]` for consistency with the code style standard.

issues.title: Missing layout() method
issues.description: Code style rule #3 lists the standard method order including `layout`. The conanfile.py does not define a `layout()` method, relying on Conan 2.x default layout. This is functionally acceptable but deviates from the recommended structure.
issues.recommendation: Add an explicit `layout()` method if the project convention requires it, or document that default layout is acceptable.

summary: Round 2 audit of duf 0.9.1 Conan recipe. All 3 P1 issues from Round 1 have been verified as fixed: (1) conandata.yml has a single official GitHub URL with no manual mirrors, (2) manifest.yaml tar_format is 'tar.gz' matching the actual .tar.gz archive, (3) test_package [PLACEHOLDER] detection is unconditional in the test() method flow. Deception detection checks (highest priority) all pass: R34 genuine binary dependency verified (test copies and runs actual duf binary from package folder), R9 no fake pass (all failure paths raise AssertionError), sha256 is 64-hex non-placeholder, R19 no pre-compiled binaries in PR, R39 source URL is official GitHub. No hardcoded Conan remote names found. commands.json present for tool type (R38). Conan 2.x API used correctly. PR is atomic (W2). No P0 or P1 issues found. Two P2 warnings (shutil.which() mode/path argument bug in _sign_elf; test_package smoke test only without platform-specific functionality verification per R40). Five P3 minor style notes. Verdict: PASS — PR is ready to merge.
